11 minutes|yungblud \u0026 halsey (feat..note: Released in February 2019, '11 Minutes' brings together the energetic alt-pop styles of YUNGBLUD and Halsey with signature heavy drum work from Blink-182's Travis Barker, creating a modern crossover that resonates with fans of classic pop-punk and rap-infused alternative music.

barrel of a gun|guster.note: "Barrel of a Gun" is a track by the Boston-derived alternative rock band Guster, known for their unique use of hand percussion instead of a traditional drum kit. As you recall from seeing them open for Barenaked Ladies in the mid-'90s, the song features the memorable "4, 3, 2, 1" hook that helped define their early acoustic-driven sound.

brick|ben folds five.note: Released in 1997 as part of Ben Folds Five's sophomore album 'Whatever and Ever Amen', 'Brick' became the band's highest-charting radio hit, proving the power of piano-driven alternative rock during a grunge-heavy era. For this listener, the song carries a special regional connection to North Carolina that felt like an uncanny sign when they eventually moved there.

colors|halsey.note: Released as the third single from Halsey's 2015 debut studio album 'Badlands', 'Colors' is a synth-heavy pop track that resonates with fans of melodic, 2010s alternative-leaning pop music.

deep cover|dr. dre and snoop dogg.note: Released in 1992 as the lead single from the soundtrack to the crime film of the same name, 'Deep Cover' marked Dr. Dre's solo debut after the breakup of N.W.A and famously introduced the world to Snoop Dogg. The track's sparse, bass-heavy G-funk beat and Snoop's effortless, laid-back delivery helped redefine West Coast hardcore rap for a new generation of listeners.

demons|imagine dragons.note: Released in 2013 as part of Imagine Dragons' debut album Night Visions, "Demons" became a massive radio hit and peaked at number six on the US Billboard Hot 100. Its soaring melody made it a defining alt-rock anthem of the 2010s, frequently heard everywhere from sports arenas to family car rides.

dreams|van halen.note: Released in 1986 on the album 5150, Van Halen's 'Dreams' prominently featured synthesizer work by Eddie Van Halen alongside Sammy Hagar's powerful vocals, capturing the era's MTV-driven sound. The track peaked at number 22 on the US Billboard Hot 100, remaining a fan favorite that bridges hard rock and synthesizer-driven melodies.

enjoy the silence|depeche mode.note: Released in 1990 on the landmark album Violator, Depeche Mode's 'Enjoy the Silence' became one of the defining synth-pop tracks of the MTV era and reached the top ten on charts across Europe and North America.

freshman|verve pipe.note: "The Freshman" by The Verve Pipe became a massive alternative rock hit in 1997, peaking at number five on the US Billboard Hot 100 and becoming a defining track of late-90s melancholic rock. For this listener, the song is indelibly tied to a painful period of early adulthood surrounding a near-breakup and a first-time visit to a friend's post-college home.

heartspark dollarsign|everclear.note: "Heartspark Dollarsign" is a single by alternative rock band Everclear, originally featured on their 1995 platinum-selling album Sparkle and Fade. Hearing this track brings back memories of an era-ending concert in Boston where the band played a memorable half-acoustic, half-rock set at an Xmas Rave with a college roommate.

here comes a regular|the replacements.note: Originally released on The Replacements' acclaimed 1985 album Tim, "Here Comes a Regular" is a poignant acoustic ballad written by Paul Westerberg that has since become a fan favorite. It serves as a fitting soundtrack for your memories of Wilmington, connecting the bittersweet nostalgia of the song with your trips there with Mike and Jess and your later One Tree Hill set tour.

hey ya|outkast.note: Released in 2003 as part of Outkast's ambitious double album Speakerboxxx/The Love Below, "Hey Ya!" became a defining pop-culture phenomenon and spent nine consecutive weeks at number one on the Billboard Hot 100. The track's infectious energy and iconic music video left a lasting impression on listeners, often evoking nostalgic memories from that era.

home sweet home|mötley crüe.note: Released in 1985 on Mötley Cröe's album Theatre of Pain, 'Home Sweet Home' helped popularize the heavy metal power ballad era of the 1980s. The track reached number 89 on the Billboard Hot 100 and remains a defining anthem for the listener, capturing the bittersweet feeling of transitioning to middle school and moving on.

i write sins not tragedies|panic! at the.note: Released in 2005 by Las Vegas band Panic! At The Disco, this theatrical rock anthem became a defining mid-2000s hit with its massive hooks and unforgettable music video. As you noted, its emo-adjacent flair captured a whole new wave of rock taking over the era, sitting right alongside tracks like Fall Out Boy's 'Thnks fr th Mmrs'.

i'll be|edwin mccain.note: Released in 1997 on Edwin McCain's album 'Misguided Roses', 'I's Be' became a major adult contemporary and Billboard Hot 100 hit. For this listener, the song captures the bittersweet feeling of friendships stretching across distance as college roommates moved away to start new lives and families.

joey|concrete blonde.note: Released in 1990 on Concrete Blonde's album 'Free', 'Joey' became the alternative rock band's biggest commercial hit, spending multiple weeks at the top of the Billboard Modern Rock Tracks chart.

love song|the cure.note: Released in 1989 as the second single from The Cure's landmark eighth studio album, *Disintegration*, 'Lovesong' became the band's highest-charting single on the US Billboard Hot 100, peaking at number two. Blending a modern, shimmering guitar sound with deeply romantic and poetic lyricism, it remains one of the defining alternative rock tracks of the era. This listener discovered the track on MTV before a college roommate further introduced them to the rich sounds of British alternative music, including The Smiths.

mayonaise|smashing pumpkins.note: Released in 1993 on The Smashing Pumpkins' breakthrough sophomore album, Siamese Dream, 'Mayonaise' became a defining alternative rock anthem known for its dynamic shift from delicate acoustic passages to heavy, layered electric guitars. For this listener and their college roommate, the track holds a special memory tied to seeing the band live at Lollapalooza.

monsters (feat. blackbear)|all time low.note: Bridging All Time Low's pop-punk roots with the 2020s landscape, "Monsters" featuring blackbear became a massive crossover hit, spending a record-breaking number of weeks at number one on the Billboard Alternative Airplay chart.

more than words|extreme.note: Extreme's acoustic ballad "More than Words" became a defining anthem for the end of high school and proms like yours, eventually topping the US Billboard Hot 100 in 1991. Formed in Boston, the rock band surprised fans by stripping away their usual electric guitar-heavy sound for this harmonious track. It remains a poignant soundtrack for moving on to college and new beginnings.

my name is jonas|weezer.note: "My Name Is Jonas" serves as the explosive opening track to Weezer's iconic 1994 self-titled debut, known as the Blue Album. As you noted, the song memorably transitions from a gentle acoustic intro into a heavy, melodic geek-rock anthem that helped define the Boston-era alternative scene.

nightswimming|r.e.m..note: Released in 1993 as part of R.E.M.'s critically acclaimed album *Automatic for the People*, "Nightswimming" is a poignant track driven primarily by Michael Stipe's vocals and Bill Berry's piano. It holds deep personal resonance for you as a wedding song for close college friends, evoking joyful memories while tying back to your own experiences of love, friendship, and first discovering alternative music.

papercut|linkin park.note: Released as the third single from Linkin Park's diamond-certified 2000 debut album 'Hybrid Theory', 'Papercut' perfectly encapsulates the band's groundbreaking fusion of aggressive rock and hip-hop. For many listeners navigating massive life transitions, the track's frantic energy and themes of paranoia served as an essential bridge between entirely different musical and social worlds.

regret|new order.note: Released in 1983... Wait, Regret was actually released in 1993 as the lead single from New Order's album Republic, becoming a major alternative radio and chart hit. For this listener, the track evokes memories of discovering '80s British alternative in college around 1993 while rooming with someone who shared that passion.

scenario|a tribe called quest.note: Released in 1992 as the final single from A Tribe Called Quest's acclaimed sophomore album "The Low End Theory," "Scenario" became an iconic hip-hop classic best known for introducing Busta Rhymes' legendary breakout guest verse. Despite the rising tide of grunge in the early 90s, the track's hard-hitting beats and explosive vocal energy kept it in heavy rotation for dorm rooms and rap fans alike.

silent running|mike + the mechanics.note: Released in late 1985 as the lead single from Mike + The Mechanics' self-titled debut album, "Silent Running" reached number six on the US Billboard Hot 100 in 1986. For this listener, the atmospheric keyboards of the track evoke powerful nostalgia for Prospect Street, childhood friendships, and a lifelong love of sports that endures to this day.

smells like teen spirit|nirvana.note: Released in 1991 as the lead single from Nirvana's seminal album Nevermind, this grunge anthem propelled the band to mainstream success and peaked at number six on the Billboard Hot 100 in early 1992. For this listener, the track serves as a soundtrack to the stark transitions of freshman year, capturing the feeling of dorm life, financial struggle, and the shifting dynamics of childhood friendships meeting college realities.

so what'cha want|beastie boys.note: Released in 1992 as the lead single from the Beastie Boys' third album, 'Check Your Head,' 'So What'Cha Want' bridged the gap between the group's hardcore punk origins and their signature hip-hop sound. The track peaked at number 68 on the US Billboard Hot 100 and helped define the alternative rap-rock crossover that resonated with fans navigating the changing musical landscape of the early '90s.

someday i suppose|mighty mighty bosstone.note: Released in 1993 on Mercury Records as the lead single from the Mighty Mighty Bosstones' second album, "Don't Know How to Party," this track helped define the Boston-born band's signature blend of hardcore punk and upbeat ska. For this listener, the song's intense and catchy energy is forever linked to a sweaty New Year's Eve concert in the basement of Cambridge's iconic Middle East club.

something's always wrong|toad the wet sp.note: "Something's Always Wrong" is a single by alternative rock band Toad the Wet Sprocket from their 1994 platinum-selling album *Dulcinea*, which reached number 12 on the Billboard Modern Rock Tracks chart. For this listener, the song is deeply tied to college BFFs, memories of seeing the band at the Orpheum Theater, and a soundtrack of consistency from their twenties until the present.

somewhere only we know|keane.note: Released in 2004 as the lead single from Keane's debut album "Hopes and Fears," "Somewhere Only We Know" became a defining melodic piano-rock anthem of the 2000s and reached number three on the UK Singles Chart. Years later, the song found a new generation of listeners through popular television features, including a memorable cover on the musical-comedy series Glee.

summer|buffalo tom.note: Buffalo Tom released "Summer" on their 1993 critically acclaimed album "Let Me Come Over," which helped cement the Boston alternative rock band's reputation for driving, emotionally resonant melodies. For this listener, the song is deeply intertwined with a poignant memory of Greg getting pulled up on stage at a concert, marking their final Buffalo Tom show together before Greg moved to Arizona.

teenage love|slick rick.note: Released in 1988 on Slick Rick's acclaimed debut album 'The Great Adventures of Slick Rick', 'Teenage Love' captured the awkwardness and earnest longing of high school romance that many listeners, including you, deeply related to during their formative years.

the old apartment|barenaked ladies.note: Released in 1996 as part of Barenaked Ladies' album Born on a Pirate Ship, 'The Old Apartment' became a major alternative rock hit and reached number one on the Canadian charts. For this listener, the track evokes memories of a post-college concert with friends featuring Guster, as well as the Arlington apartment where their future wife once lived while they were nearby in Waltham.

there is a light that never goes out|the.note: Introduced by a college roommate during junior year, this listener connected deeply with the confident vocals and clever lyrics of The Smiths. Released in 1992 as a single from 'The Queen Is Dead' era compilations and later widely acclaimed, 'There Is a Light That Never Goes Out' remains one of the band's most enduring and celebrated anthems.

thnks fr th mmrs|fall out boy.note: Released in 2007 from Fall Out Boy's album "Infinity on High," this high-energy track became a massive mainstream success, peaking at number 11 on the Billboard Hot 100. Its infectious hooks and dramatic flair made it a defining staple of the mid-2000s pop-punk era.

tiny dancer|elton john.note: Released in 1971 on Elton John's album 'Madman Across the Water', 'Tiny Dancer' features iconic backing vocals and has become one of the artist's signature tracks. The song gained a massive cultural resurgence decades later, famously featured in the tour bus sing-along scene in Cameron Crowe's 2000 film 'Almost Famous'—a moment that clearly resonates with your own memories of music and friendship.

title and registration|death cab for cut.note: Released as the second single from Death Cab for Cutie's 2005 major-label debut, Plans, "Title and Registration" showcases the band's signature melodic, quiet indie rock sound. The track resonated with fans through witty lyricism, including its memorable opening observation about the glove compartment. This thoughtful songwriting helped propel Plans to a peak of No. 4 on the US Billboard 200 and earned the album a Grammy nomination for Best Alternative Music Album.

welcome to the terrordome|public enemy.note: Released in 1989 as the lead single from Public Enemy's landmark album 'Fear of a Black Planet', 'Welcome to the Terrordome' is celebrated for its dense, high-energy production and intricate lyricism. For this listener, the track evokes nostalgic memories of car rides to the amusement park with family, alongside the enduring impact of discovering hip-hop through their cousin.

with or without you|u2.note: Released in 1987 on U2's landmark album *The Joshua Tree*, "With or Without You" became the band's first number-one single on the US Billboard Hot 100. During your time living in Boston, the city's strong Irish cultural ties made it feel as though the band had been warmly adopted by the local music scene. The track remains enduringly powerful, driven by its soaring vocals, emotional lyrics, and innovative guitar textures.

would|alice in chains.note: Alice in Chains' "Would?" was written by Jerry Cantrell as a tribute to the late Mother Love Bone singer Andrew Wood, and it became a standout track on the 1992 soundtrack for Cameron Crowe's Seattle-set film Singles. As you remember from sophomore year, the song helped define the era's grunge movement and peaked at number 31 on the Billboard Mainstream Rock Tracks chart.
